To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structural history of the Front Royal area of the Blue Ridge in northern Virginia includes the following events in this order: (1) folding, (2) cleavage, (3) superimposed folding, (4) fracture cleavage, and (5) fracturing.

the structural history of the Precambrian and Paleozoic rocks of the Front Royal area is characterized by: 1) a sequence of tectonic structures related by displacement directions oriented in a northwest - southeast plane, and 2) a kinematic uniformity in the principal stress directions during deformation.

the Blue Ridge uplift of northern Virginia is a Paleozoic fold belt that experienced regional greenschist metamorphism and deformation accompanied by cleavage, lineation, superimposed folding, and fracturing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural geology of a portion of the Blue Ridge in Northern Virginia.
the structure of a portion of the Blue Ridge in the Front Royal area of northern Virginia.
the structural geology of a small area in the Front Royal, Virginia vicinity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a Paleozoic diachronous orogeny of regional extent affected the Front Royal area.

the Blue Ridge of the Front Royal area was a site of Paleozoic deformation, and the deformation was characterized by folding, slaty cleavage, and lineation, by superimposed folds with fracture cleavage and striated fractures, and by reverse faults, high angle longitudinal faults, high angle transverse faults, zones of en echelion tension fractures, and by a kinematically uniform northwest-southeast displacement direction.
the Blue Ridge of Northern Virginia was deformed by one major diastrophic event during the Paleozoicrocks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Front Royal area is a part of the Blue Ridge which experienced regional metamorphism, folding, and faulting during the Paleozoicoic.
the Blue Ridge of the Front Royal area was a zone of compression in a northwest-southwest direction.
a single diastrophism produced a series of structures which were superimposed upon each other and which were related to each other kinematically.

the Blue Ridge of Virginia was a major thrust belt during the Paleozoicoic.
the Blue Ridge was deformed by a single event that was characterized by a constant direction of principal stress.
